plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers held above the foliage. It is widely cultivated in gardens and fields and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and huge flower heads composed of golden ray florets surrounding a central disc of tiny seed-producing florets. Early varieties begin blooming in early July across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and the United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west (heliotropism), but mature flower heads stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial of the daisy family with drooping pinkish-purple petals around a spiky, copper-orange central cone. It thrives in prairies and open woodlands and is a favorite of pollinators and goldfinches.
plants.location: Central and eastern United States prairies and open woods; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiky central cone.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, featuring a bowl of stiff pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central dome of tiny flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it flowers in the cooler months and into winter and spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through spring in South Africa, with flowering often beginning in winter (around June to July onward)
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western Cape and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after Proteus, the Greek god who could change his shape.
